rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act statewide rent cap
rules.requirement: For a covered unit, your landlord cannot raise your rent by more than 5% plus local CPI, or 10%, whichever is lower, in any 12-month period, measured from the lowest rent charged in the prior 12 months. If you stay in the unit, the rent can be raised no more than twice in 12 months, and the landlord can set any starting rent for a new tenancy.
rules.key_value: lesser of 5% + CPI or 10% per 12 months

coverage.summary: Most residential rental units in California, including mobilehome park units. Exempt: housing that received a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (except mobilehomes); deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing; school or college dormitories; units under stricter local rent control; separately alienable single-family homes or condos whose owner is not a REIT, corporation or LLC with a corporate member, if the tenant got the required written exemption notice; and owner-occupied two-unit buildings where neither unit is an ADU or JADU.
minor_exemptions_not_in_data: Dormitories owned and operated by higher-education institutions or K-12 schools
Separately alienable single-family homes or condos not owned by a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member, with written exemption notice to tenant

rules.exemptions: Initial rent for a new tenancy is not capped. Exempt: affordable housing restricted by deed or agreement; school/college dormitories; housing under local rent control that restricts increases below this cap; housing issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years (unless a mobilehome); separately alienable units (e.g., single-family homes, condos) not owned by a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management, with the required written notice to tenants; owner-occupied duplexes (no ADU/JADU) while the owner continues in occupancy; homeowners of a mobilehome.
rules.penalty: Tenant may sue for injunctive relief, damages equal to the overcharge, discretionary attorney's fees and costs, and up to three times the overcharge for willful, oppressive, fraudulent or malicious conduct; Attorney General and city attorney or county counsel may enforce. Three-year limitations period. Waivers are void.
rules.quoted_span: Subject to subdivision (b), an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.
rules.interaction: Does not apply to housing under a valid local rent control ordinance (consistent with Costa-Hawkins, Civ. Code § 1954.50 et seq.) that restricts annual increases below this cap. The section is not intended to expand or limit local authority to regulate rents. It applies to rent increases on or after March 15, 2019, with the applicable rent reset on January 1, 2020, and to mobilehome tenancies for increases on or after February 18, 2021. The current text was repealed and re-added by Stats. 2023, Ch. 290 (SB 567), effective January 1, 2024 and operative April 1, 2024. It is repealed as of January 1, 2030.

notes: Official code text of Civ. Code § 1947.12 as amended by SB 567 (2023). Effective date is taken from the transition clause in subdivision (h) (applicable rent on January 1, 2020; increases covered from March 15, 2019), not from the SB 567 operative date of April 1, 2024. The just-cause statute (§ 1946.2) is mentioned only in the exemption-notice text and is not extracted here. The section sunsets January 1, 2030.
